items.signal_prefix: Full-year forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 (FY

set.signal: Full-year forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 (FY3/27; deck): net sales JPY 1,690.0 billion (+1.5%) and operating income JPY 120.0 billion (+15.4%; includes approximately JPY 2.6 billion of restructuring costs) kept unchanged 'from a conservative perspective' (first half JPY 846.5 billion / JPY 53.0 billion, second half JPY 843.5 billion / JPY 67.0 billion); profit before taxes JPY 118.0 billion; profit attributable to owners of the parent revised upward to JPY 87.0 billion (EPS JPY 216.64; +17.8% against FY3/26 excluding special factors). Segment forecasts (net sales / operating income): Precision Technologies JPY 313.0 billion (+11.3%) / JPY 70.0 billion (+12.5%); Motor, Lighting & Sensing JPY 492.0 billion (+7.8%) / JPY 31.0 billion (+15.1%); Semiconductor & Electronics JPY 530.0 billion (-10.2%) / JPY 28.0 billion (+5.0%); Access Solutions JPY 350.0 billion (+5.3%) / JPY 18.5 billion (+8.3%). Sub-segment sales forecasts: ball bearings JPY 198.5 billion, aerospace JPY 82.5 billion, PMC JPY 32.0 billion; motors JPY 376.0 billion, electronic devices JPY 77.0 billion, sensing devices JPY 39.0 billion. Capex forecast JPY 95.0 billion and depreciation and amortisation JPY 75.0 billion (FY3/26: JPY 96.5 billion and JPY 70.4 billion); assumed rate US$1 = JPY 155.00 for Q2-Q4. CEO Kainuma: the strong Q1 did not lead to a raise because the company was criticised in the past for raising forecasts early in the term and then missing; given the uncertain macro environment it kept the initial guidance out of an extremely conservative approach.
